questions.question: With a manual transmission, how can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To prevent rolling backward when starting, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal. Use the parking brake if needed to keep your vehicle from rolling back.

questions.question: If a driver coming toward you is using high beam headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Look directly at the headlights.
Flash your high beam lights to tell the driver to switch to low beams.
Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
Pull to the side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
questions.explanation: When an oncoming vehicle uses high beam headlights, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road. This prevents the bright lights from blinding you.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail for two main reasons. Which one is correct?

options.text: Loss of hydraulic pressure in the system.
Driving uphill.
Brakes get too cold.
Brakes are used too much in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of hydraulic pressure in the system.
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failures usually happen for two reasons. The first is overusing brakes on a downgrade, which causes them to fade. The second is a loss of hydraulic pressure in the braking system. Well-maintained brakes rarely fail, but you should know what to do if they do.

questions.question: Starting in which year did new trailers have to have ABS?
questions.explanation: Starting March 1, 1998, all new trailers and converter dollies must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allows wheels to lock up.
Stops wheels from locking up.
Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.
Helps operate the brake lights.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) keeps a vehicle's wheels from locking up during hard braking.

questions.question: Why is proper coupling technique important?

options.text: It is the same on all vehicles.
It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
It means the fifth wheel plate should not be greased.
It can be learned over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: Knowing how to properly couple and uncouple combination vehicles is critical for safe operation. Improper coupling is dangerous.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Cracked drums
Brake shoes with oil or grease on them
Brake shoes worn very thin
Brake pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: Signs of brake problems include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or dangerously worn thin.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Look at the tires.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires connected to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do if the air pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: Continue driving normally.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.
Call local law enforcement.
Safely leave the road and stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely leave the road and stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on, stop immediately and safely park your vehicle. This warning means there is a problem in the air brake system that needs repair.

questions.question: What does heavy steering often indicate?

options.text: Rear tire failure.
Front tire failure.
A shifting load.
Coolant overheating.

questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means one of your front tires has failed. If you notice a change in steering, safely exit the road as soon as possible and check your tires.

questions.question: What can rough acceleration do?

options.text: Can damage a vehicle.
Is necessary to warm up engine parts.
Improves gas mileage.
Should be done on slippery surfaces.

questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine.

questions.question: If you pull off to the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Let your taillights alert other drivers.
Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
Keep your lights off so you don't distract other drivers.
Keep your door open to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. This is especially important at night. Taillights alone are not enough because other drivers might think your vehicle is moving normally and hit it.

questions.question: Trailers with low clearance underneath may be hard to drive:

options.text: On interstate highways.
Over railroad crossings.
On dirt roads.
At the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: Railroad crossings may be hard to cross when pulling a trailer with low clearance. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors with long trailers have the most difficulty crossing raised crossings.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downhill.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when transporting cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause air to leak out of the brake system, which makes the brakes release. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, the maximum air loss for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes is ____ per minute.

options.text: 3 psi
5 psi
7 psi
9 psi

questions.explanation: When testing a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, air should not leak faster than 5 psi per minute. If air leaks faster, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: A double or triple trailer:

options.text: Can usually be driven faster than a straight truck.
Is usually less stable than smaller commercial vehicles.
Is always easier to drive than other commercial vehicles.
Does not need a special endorsement to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually less stable than smaller commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Double and triple trailers are less stable than single commercial vehicles. They are more likely to roll over. Drive them very smoothly and gently to prevent rollovers.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often can:

options.text: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
Add more air to the brake system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.
Make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often releases air faster than the compressor can add it back.

questions.question: Emergency equipment, such as a fire extinguisher, is:

options.text: Only needed for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Only needed for interstate travel.
Required.
Only required when carrying passengers.

questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective warning triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to cause hydroplaning?

options.text: Tires with worn tread
Properly inflated tires
New tires
Traveling under 10 mph

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely on wet roads with worn tire tread or low tire pressure. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.

options.text: Is easier
Requires more driving skill
Is better for training
Is safer in bad weather

questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are longer and heavier.
